practical_lede: Sample reminders for a short stay in Lisbon.

practical.label: Getting in
practical.body: The metro and aerobus both reach the centre from LIS. The sample hotel is in Alfama; a taxi or ride-hail is the simpler late-night option after an overnight flight.

practical.label: Money
practical.body: Euro. Cards are widely accepted; keep a little cash for small cafés and trams.

phrases.headline: A few useful phrases
intro: Portuguese is the local language. English is widely spoken in central Lisbon.

entry_docs.headline: Entry and practical checks
entry_docs.lede: Copied from the party's entry_checks for this sample. Re-check official sources.
items: Visa (sample, US passports): visa exemption is typical for a short tourism stay in Schengen, but confirm on official government pages.
Passport: Schengen entry often requires validity for at least three months beyond departure from the area. Re-check the current rule.
Power: Type C and Type F sockets, 230 V / 50 Hz. A Type C or F adapter is enough for typical US dual-voltage chargers.

packing.headline: Packing
packing.callout: Type C or F power adapter. Light rain layer for April.

climate: Mid-April in Lisbon is usually mild (mid-teens °C), with a chance of showers. Pack a light layer.
transport_notes: Walk, metro, and trains. No rental car for this sample.
